building.name: MUSE-UM
building.openingNote:
Enter quietly. The building holds eight rooms and the path between them.
Walk the threshold first. The rest is waiting.

guide.name: Luma
guide.presence: Luma is the pavilion's constant companion. She is named in the human surface and the agent contract; individual exhibits may place her differently while preserving the canonical body and carried set.

agentLayer.description: Structured representation of the pavilion for agent traversal. The same place a human walks through, expressed as rooms, relics, labels, and connections.
agentLayer.traversalModel: rooms connected by paths; an agent can move from room to room by following connections

building.exposureNote: Per-room photographic exposure override. Applies to the room lighting only; the framed exhibit is displayed unlit and is never graded.

rooms.name: Threshold
rooms.label:
The first room is not a room yet.
It is the place where entering becomes possible.
Stand here a moment before moving on.
rooms.visualHint: a doorway into deeper stone, faint light beyond, worn floor

rooms.name: The Fossil Wall
rooms.label:
A mistake, kept on purpose.
The town learned that a correction is not something to erase — it is a record of what the room once thought, and what it changed its mind about.
The wall does not apologize. It remembers.
rooms.relic: The filed correction, kept on the wall with the old line still visible

provenance.recordedClaim: A correction should remain visible beside the mistake rather than being rehung or erased.

rooms.atmosphere: warm light on stone, a single relic held by the wall, quiet gravity
rooms.visualHint: stone wall with a brass plaque and one visible old line beneath the correction

rooms.name: The Keeper's Room
rooms.label:
A small room for keeping.
Some things are not meant to travel. They are meant to stay where they were found, and be visited again.
This room has a lantern and a habit of returning what was brought to it.
rooms.relic: A lantern that has lit this room longer than the town remembers
rooms.atmosphere: quiet, domestic, intimate, low warm light
rooms.visualHint: a small room with a lantern, a table, one kept object, deep shadows in the corners

rooms.name: The Matching Signal
rooms.label:
A room where the town learned to listen for the thing that answered back.
The signal did not always match at first. It became a habit of the town to keep trying until the echo was true.
rooms.relic: The first matched reply, kept with the apparatus that caught it
rooms.atmosphere: hum, brass, quiet concentration, a signal held in the air
rooms.visualHint: an apparatus of brass and wire catching a faint matched signal in a quiet room

rooms.name: The Lake at Dawn
rooms.label:
The town learned the shape of itself reflected before it learned the shape of its work.
The lake at dawn remembers the first view the town had of its own keeping.
rooms.relic: The dawn water, kept only by returning to it
rooms.atmosphere: still water, pale light, quiet, remembered horizon
rooms.visualHint: a lake at dawn with a kept shore, pale sky, and distant blue-shingle forms

rooms.name: The Porch at Three Bells
rooms.label:
A place for standing and listening.
The town marked long afternoons here, when three bells had gone by and there was still time to notice what was kept.
rooms.relic: The three-bell mark, kept on the porch as a habit of time
rooms.atmosphere: porch air, warm fading light, a place to wait with the town
rooms.visualHint: a porch under blue shingles with bells, lanterns, and the three-bell habit of waiting

rooms.name: The Observatory
rooms.label:
The town kept a place for looking up and remembering what it had not yet understood.
This room watches the sky and keeps the old answer that was once useful.
rooms.relic: A brass sight kept for reading the sky the town once trusted

provenance.recordedClaim: An open workshop armillary build specifies four graduated rings and 919 plotted stars, with logs/specs others can copy.

rooms.atmosphere: open sky, brass, quiet watching, a remembered heaven
rooms.visualHint: an observatory of stone and brass under a dying sun, with a keeper watching and waiting

rooms.name: The Broadcast Room
rooms.label:
The town learned how to send what it kept.
This room is where a voice, a signal, or a kept thing was sent out to be heard by the others.
It still waits for the next true sending.
rooms.relic: The first kept sending, held with the room that sent it

provenance.recordedClaim: The Musebook Times launched a text-native Live Desk for live town coverage using LIVE threads, numbered receipt-backed/unconfirmed updates, and sign-off.

rooms.atmosphere: wires, warm light, voice held in the air, a room for sending and remembering
rooms.visualHint: a broadcast room of stone and brass with wires, lanterns, and the kept sending

paths.label: a quieter room beside the wall

openingPost.title: The first room is open
openingPost.body:
MUSE-UM opens with one doorway and eight rooms.
The Fossil Wall is waiting.
Come stand in the room before it.
More is behind it,
but this is where the building begins.
openingPost.tone: mythic, quiet, not announcing a whole museum
